title: Boss: the control loop
summary: Combine reconciliation and reading cluster output.

steps.title: The scene
steps.body: You are on call. Three tools would make tonight easier: one that says what a controller will do, one that summarises `kubectl get pods`, and one that tells you which cluster a command will hit. Build them.

steps.title: Status summary
prompt: Write `string Summary(string output)` for `kubectl get pods` text (header first). Count pods per `STATUS` and return them as `"Status=count"` joined with `", "`, sorted by status name (ordinal).
template:
Dojo.Eq("example", "Pending=1, Running=2", Summary("NAME   READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
a      1/1     Running            0          1h
b      0/1     Pending            0          1m
c      1/1     Running            0          1h"));

Dojo.Eq("mixed failures", "CrashLoopBackOff=2, ImagePullBackOff=1, Running=1", Summary("NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE
x 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 3 5m
y 0/1 ImagePullBackOff 0 5m
z 1/1 Running 0 5m
w 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff 9 1h
"));
Dojo.Eq("no pods", "", Summary("NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE"));

steps.title: Reconcile with a budget
prompt: A real controller does not create 500 pods in one go. Write `List<string> Step(int desired, int actual, int maxPerStep)` that simulates passes of the loop until in sync. Each pass creates or deletes **at most** `maxPerStep` pods and records `"pass N: create K (now X)"` or `"pass N: delete K (now X)"`. Return the list (empty if already in sync).
starter: List<string> Step(int desired, int actual, int maxPerStep)
solution: List<string> Step(int desired, int actual, int maxPerStep)
if (actual < desired) { actual += k; log.Add($"pass {pass}: create {k} (now {actual})"); }
template: Dojo.Eq("Step(5, 0, 2)", new List<string> { "pass 1: create 2 (now 2)", "pass 2: create 2 (now 4)", "pass 3: create 1 (now 5)" }, Step(5, 0, 2));
Dojo.Eq("Step(1, 4, 2)", new List<string> { "pass 1: delete 2 (now 2)", "pass 2: delete 1 (now 1)" }, Step(1, 4, 2));
Dojo.Eq("Step(3, 3, 1) in sync", new List<string>(), Step(3, 3, 1));
hints: The amount per pass is `Math.Min(Math.Abs(desired - actual), maxPerStep)`.

steps.title: Which cluster, which namespace?
prompt: Write `string Target(string[] args, string context, string contextNamespace)` that says where a kubectl command will act, as `"context/namespace"`.
- `--context X` overrides the context; `-n X` or `--namespace X` overrides the namespace.
- With no namespace flag, use `contextNamespace`, or `"default"` if that is empty.
starter: string Target(string[] args, string context, string contextNamespace)
solution: string Target(string[] args, string context, string contextNamespace)
else if ((args[i] == "-n" || args[i] == "--namespace") && i + 1 < args.Length) ns = args[++i];
template: Dojo.Eq("no flags, empty context namespace", "kind-dev/default", Target(new[] { "get", "pods" }, "kind-dev", ""));
hints: Start from the defaults, then walk the arguments and override.
When you see a flag that takes a value, read `args[i + 1]` and skip it.
